sources_quoted.docs/math-foundations.md :: survival-wal: Shield absorption (survival walk): clipping identity absorbed = min(shield, damage), overkill = max(0, damage-absorbed), absorbed+overkill = damage -- EXACT. The heal split is the same clipping identity against the health pool: applied = min(amount, max_health - current_health), overheal = amount - applied, applied + overheal = amount.

rounding_analysis.exact_delta_form: The tightest form needs no absolute reconstruction at all. Health is full immediately after member 4 ([31]) in BOTH trees -- its overheal is 32.6 pre and 46.7 post, both strictly positive, read off the record itself. Every heal between t=3.23 and the member is unmoved in amount and un-clipped in both trees, so it contributes identically on both sides and cancels. Therefore delta(applied[39]) = delta(window damage) = (-75.5) + 7.6 + 7.6 = -60.3 exactly. 271.4 - 60.3 = 211.1 and 88.0 + 60.3 = 148.3, from only THREE rounded deltas, budget +/-0.15. mechanism.why_the_window_damage_fell: Two independent, opposite-signed item fixes land inside the (3.23, 4.31] window. (1) Black Cleaver Carve de-duplication. The passive reads 'Each stack inflicts 6% armor reduction, up to 30% at 5 stacks' with 'Non-basic damage dealt on the same target may apply stacks only once per frame'. Pre-change the ally's autos on the healed unit escalate 41.4 / 50.7 / 90.1 / 128.9 as stacks over-accumulated; post-change they settle 41.4 / 45.9 / 53.4 / 53.4 -- a saturating ladder against a 120-armor target, the shape the passive's 5-stack cap bounds. Row [46] is the big one: 128.9 -> 53.4, -75.5. (2) Bloodsong single-application Expose Weakness. The passive reads 'inflict them with Expose Weakness for 4 seconds, causing them to take 8% increased damage from all sources'. The spellblade procs at t=1.50 and t=4.50 (rows [27] and [56]); every one of the ten rises is ratio 1.080 (94.1 -> 101.7 = 1.0808; 138.6 -> 149.7 = 1.0801; 157.8 -> 170.4 = 1.0798), and rows [48] and [50] carry +7.6 each. Net over the window: -75.5 + 7.6 + 7.6 = -60.3.
mechanism.why_that_is_the_whole_question: The heal size is not in dispute -- 359.4 is re-derived exactly from wiki text above and is unmoved. The split is a pure clipping identity, applied = min(amount, room) with room = max_health - current health. The healed unit is topped off at t=3.23 in both trees, so the room at t=4.31 is exactly the window damage minus the 343.3 that the three earlier heals at the same timestamp had already restored. Less damage landed on him in that window post-change, so less room existed, so more of the same 359.4 spilled. 614.8 - 343.3 = 271.5 (pre, matching the recorded 271.4); 554.5 - 343.3 = 211.2 (post).
mechanism.why_the_series_had_to_be_adjudicated_who: Member 6 ([47], t=5.39) is the load-bearing one. It applies its full 359.4 with overheal 0.0 -- it does NOT top the pool off -- so its window's +26.3 delta does not terminate there. It is carried across t=5.39 and is the entire reason member 7 moves (261.8 -> 287.9) despite both damage rows inside member 7's own window being unmoved. Members 1 and 2 are unmoved not by accident but because the Bloodsong spellblade has not yet procced and the Carve ladder has not yet diverged. Members 3, 4 and 5 move in three different directions and magnitudes (+15.4, -13.9, -60.3) purely from which of the two item fixes dominates their window. The series is one health path; only the whole path is well-posed, which is exactly what the R-15/R-18 repeated-source amendment requires.
